steps.title: Tavel
steps.body: Tavel, across the river from Châteauneuf, is France's only appellation for rosé alone. Its rosé is darker and fuller than Provence's, made from Grenache, Cinsault and others with longer skin contact. It's a rosé for food, able to age a few years. Lirac, nearby, makes red, white and rosé.

steps.title: Sweet wines
steps.body: Beaumes-de-Venise makes Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise, a vin doux naturel: fermentation is stopped by adding grape spirit, keeping natural sugar, at 15% or more alcohol. It's golden, with orange blossom, peach and grape. Rasteau also makes a fortified Grenache vin doux naturel, red or amber.

steps.prompt: What is a vin doux naturel?
options: A wine fortified during fermentation to keep sugar
steps.explanation: Spirit stops the yeast, leaving natural sweetness.

steps.title: The crus
steps.body: Besides Châteauneuf and Tavel, the southern Rhône crus include Gigondas, Vacqueyras, Rasteau, Cairanne, Vinsobres, Lirac and Beaumes-de-Venise. Below them sit Côtes du Rhône Villages, sometimes with a village name, and then Côtes du Rhône. Each step up means stricter rules and usually more character.

steps.explanation: Hermitage is in the northern Rhône.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Crus sit above Villages and Côtes du Rhône
